title: API (a server other programs talk to)
fits: A JSON API for an app, a webhook receiver, or a backend for a phone or desktop app, with its own data.
notFor: more than one server at once (the database is one file on one server)
pages people look at (use the web app or website recipe)

stack.choice: JavaScript (ES modules) on Node.js 22 or newer
stack.why: Nothing to compile; tests run with Node's own test runner.

stack.choice: Fastify 5, set up by the official fastify-cli
stack.why: Fast, widely used, with request validation built in.
Safe headers and a cap on requests from one caller, from the first route.

stack.choice: SQLite through better-sqlite3, with Drizzle for queries and migrations
stack.why: One file, no database server; queries that can't be injected.

after.do: Register @fastify/helmet and @fastify/rate-limit as plugins in plugins/ (one file each, like plugins/sensible.js), with a test that a response carries the headers and that the limit answers 429.

host.name: Any Node.js host with a lasting disk, running one copy
host.deploy: npm ci --omit=dev, then npm start with the database file on the lasting disk. Set up by /starter-kit:launch; not part of the recipe test.

accounts.name: GitHub
accounts.why: Holds the code and runs the checks on every push.

accounts.name: A hosting account (one server with a lasting disk)
accounts.why: Runs the API and keeps the database file.

settings.name: PORT
settings.why: The port the host expects; fastify-cli reads FASTIFY_PORT or PORT.

notes: Files in plugins/ and routes/ are loaded automatically by @fastify/autoload; a folder under routes/ becomes a path prefix. Shared things (database, auth) are plugins wrapped in fastify-plugin so every route sees them.
Give every route a JSON schema for its body, query and params: Fastify then rejects bad input before your code runs and responses only include the fields in the response schema.
Tests build the app with test/helper.js and call app.inject(), so no port is opened. Every route gets a test for good input, bad input and a caller who isn't allowed.
This is plain JavaScript with ES modules: import/export, file extensions in relative imports, no require.
Database changes: edit the Drizzle schema, generate a migration with drizzle-kit generate and commit it; never change the live database by hand.
SQLite means one running copy. Back up the database file and move to a database server before planning a second copy.
Never log request bodies or headers whole: they carry passwords and tokens.
